title: AnimatedSprite2D.frames becomes null immediately after assignment (despite valid resource)
body:
### Tested versions

v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Windows 11 pro, v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6], NVIDIA RTX 3050 laptop

### Issue description

Issue Description
Problem Description:
I am encountering a persistent Invalid access to property or key 'frames' on a base object of type 'AnimatedSprite2D' error in Godot Engine (v4.4.1 Standard on Windows 10). This error consistently occurs when attempting to access the frames property of an AnimatedSprite2D node. Crucially, the error happens immediately after a SpriteFrames resource has been successfully loaded and assigned to the animated_sprite.frames property. Debug logs confirm that the loaded SpriteFrames resource itself is valid and contains the expected animations (e.g., 5 animations like "idle", "run", "attack", "die", "walk"). However, upon the very next attempt to interact with animated_sprite.frames (e.g., to retrieve animation names or perform a null check), the property is found to be null or invalid, leading to the reported error. This behavior suggests that either the AnimatedSprite2D node itself becomes invalid, or its frames property is unexpectedly reset or deallocated, immediately after the assignment.

Troubleshooting Steps Attempted and Their Outcomes:

Extensive debugging and troubleshooting steps have been performed, consistently yielding the same error behavior:

Initial Syntax Errors (Parse error):

Description: The project initially failed to launch due to Parse error in main.gd and main_menu_ui.gd.
Outcome: Syntax errors (e.g., missing colons, incorrect indentation) were identified and corrected. This resolved the Parse error and allowed the project to launch, revealing the Invalid access to property or key 'frames' error.
gameConfig.json and SpriteFrames Consistency Check:

Description: Verified that sprite_frames_path in gameConfig.json was correct (res://assets/test1.tres or res://assets/test_temp_frames.tres). Ensured available_animations in JSON exactly matched the animation names within the .tres file (e.g., removing knight01/ prefixes).
Outcome: JSON loading and parsing were confirmed successful; animation names were correctly matched. This was not the root cause.
Enhanced Script Debugging (student_character.gd):

Description: Added numerous print() statements and is_instance_valid() checks throughout the script to monitor variable states and node validity at critical execution points.
Outcome: animated_sprite was confirmed valid (is_instance_valid(animated_sprite) returns true) prior to the frames assignment. The loaded SpriteFrames resource (e.g., loaded_frames or _loaded_sprite_frames) was also confirmed valid and contained correct animation data. Despite this, the error consistently occurred at the point where animated_sprite.frames was first accessed immediately after its assignment.
Usage of await get_tree().process_frame:

Description: Introduced await get_tree().process_frame after key operations (like frames assignment) to ensure Godot had sufficient time for internal processing and node readiness.
Outcome: No change in behavior; the error persisted at the same logical point.
Changed animated_sprite initialization from @onready to _ready():

Description: Modified the animated_sprite variable assignment from @onready var animated_sprite = $Sprite to var animated_sprite; func _ready(): animated_sprite = $Sprite to ensure proper initialization order.
Outcome: No significant change; the error continued.
Introduced Strong Reference for SpriteFrames Resource (_loaded_sprite_frames):

Description: A member variable (_loaded_sprite_frames) was added to hold a strong reference to the loaded SpriteFrames resource, attempting to prevent premature garbage collection or resource deallocation.
Outcome: The _loaded_sprite_frames variable successfully retained the resource. However, animated_sprite.frames still became null or invalid immediately after assignment, leading to the error.
Tested with a New, Simple SpriteFrames Resource (test_temp_frames.tres):

Description: To rule out corruption or specific issues with the original test1.tres file, a brand new SpriteFrames resource (test_temp_frames.tres) with minimal frames and a single animation ("test_idle") was created and used in gameConfig.json.
Outcome: The Invalid access to property or key 'frames' error still occurred when using this new, simple resource, strongly suggesting the problem is not with the .tres file's content itself.
Clean Godot Engine Reinstallation:

Description: Performed a complete uninstallation (including user configuration files) and reinstallation of the latest Godot Engine version.
Outcome: The error persisted identically, ruling out a corrupted editor installation.
Replaced the AnimatedSprite2D Node in StudentCharacter.tscn:

Description: The existing Sprite (AnimatedSprite2D) node in StudentCharacter.tscn was deleted and a brand new AnimatedSprite2D node was added with the exact same name (Sprite), ensuring its Frames property was Empty in the Editor.
Outcome: The error remained unresolved, indicating the issue is not with a corrupted specific node instance.
Conclusion:
Given the persistence of the error across comprehensive debugging steps, resource changes, and a clean engine reinstallation, this is an highly unusual and difficult-to-diagnose issue. It strongly points towards either a subtle, underlying bug within the Godot Engine's AnimatedSprite2D and its frames property lifecycle, or an unforeseen interaction/invalidation coming from another part of the project's scene tree or scripts that is not immediately apparent in the provided code snippets.

### Steps to reproduce

Steps to Reproduce:
(Please follow these steps precisely to create a minimal project that reproduces the bug.)

Godot Version: Godot 4.241 Standard

OS/Environment: Windows 11

Create a new Godot project (e.g., named AnimatedSpriteBug).

Create StudentCharacter.tscn scene:

Right-click in the FileSystem dock -> New Scene.
Add a CharacterBody2D as the root node and name it StudentCharacter.
Add an AnimatedSprite2D node as a child of StudentCharacter and name it exactly Sprite.
Important: In the Inspector for the Sprite (AnimatedSprite2D) node, ensure the "Frames" property is Empty. Do not assign any SpriteFrames resource here.
Save this scene as res://scenes/student_character.tscn.
Attach a new GDScript to the StudentCharacter node, save it as res://scripts/student_character.gd. Paste the complete code from your latest student_character.gd into this script. (The version that includes var animated_sprite = null and the assignment in _ready(), along with _loaded_sprite_frames).
Create TestRandomCharacter.tscn scene:

Create a new scene with a Node2D as the root. Name it TestRandomCharacter.
Add an instance of student_character.tscn as a child of TestRandomCharacter.
Save this scene as res://scenes/test/TestRandomCharacter.tscn.
Attach a new GDScript to the TestRandomCharacter node, save it as res://scripts/test_random_character.gd. Paste the following minimal code into it:
GDScript

# res://scripts/test_random_character.gd
extends Node2D

@onready var student_character_instance = $"StudentCharacter" # Assuming you named the instance "StudentCharacter"

func _ready():
    # Minimal setup, assuming GlobalProfessionManager handles config loading and character data
    # For this reproduction, we'll hardcode minimal character_data
    var character_data = {
        "id": "test_animated_char",
        "name": "Nhan Vat AnimatedSprite Test",
        "sprite_frames_path": "res://assets/test_temp_frames.tres", 
        "available_animations": ["test_idle"] 
    }
    if student_character_instance:
        student_character_instance.setup_character(character_data)
    else:
        push_error("Error: student_character_instance is null.")
Create gameConfig.json:

Create a new folder named data inside your res:// directory.
Right-click on the data folder -> New TextFile. Name it gameConfig.json.
Paste the following JSON content into gameConfig.json:
JSON

{
  "professions": [
    {
      "id": "test_profession",
      "name": "Nghề Test",
      "description": "Nghề dùng de test AnimatedSprite2D.",
      "stat_priority": { "str": 0.2, "con": 0.2, "dex": 0.2, "int": 0.2, "wis": 0.2 },
      "character_types": ["test_animated_char"]
    }
  ],
  "character_types_details": [
    {
      "id": "test_animated_char",
      "name": "Nhan Vat AnimatedSprite Test",
      "sprite_frames_path": "res://assets/test_temp_frames.tres", 
      "available_animations": ["test_idle"] 
    }
  ]
}
Save gameConfig.json.
Create test_temp_frames.tres and add a basic animation:

In the FileSystem dock, right-click on the assets folder -> New Resource....
Search for and select SpriteFrames. Name it test_temp_frames.tres and save it in res://assets/.
Double-click test_temp_frames.tres to open the SpriteFrames editor.
Click the Add Animation button (the + icon). Name the new animation test_idle.
Drag and drop at least one arbitrary image file (e.g., a simple square texture, or a single frame from any sprite sheet you have) into the test_idle animation's frame area. This is just to ensure it has frames.
Save test_temp_frames.tres.
Set TestRandomCharacter.tscn as the Main Scene:

Go to Project -> Project Settings -> Application -> Run.
Set "Main Scene" to res://scenes/test/TestRandomCharacter.tscn.
Close Project Settings.
Run the project.
